title: What to Expect: First Month of the IB Diploma
summary: Expect first month IB Diploma changes with confidence. Learn what DP1 classes, workload, TOK, CAS, assessments, and study routines involve this fall term.
body_markdown:
The first month of the IB Diploma rarely feels dramatic on day one. You receive a timetable, meet teachers, open new folders, and hear several unfamiliar abbreviations. Then, almost quietly, the pace changes.


If you want to know what to **expect first month IB Diploma** , the direct answer is faster lessons, greater independence, unfamiliar assessment criteria, early subject uncertainty, and more responsibilities competing for the same afternoon. You are not expected to master the programme in September. You are expected to begin building habits that will still work when the term becomes busier.


Students who settle effectively are not necessarily those who arrive knowing the most. They are often the ones who notice how the programme works, ask precise questions, and create a simple routine before every decision feels urgent.


### Your first-month IB checklist


By the end of your first four weeks, aim to have:


- Confirmed your six subjects and their HL or SL levels
- Collected assessment outlines and internal deadlines
- Created one calendar for tests, coursework, CAS, and personal commitments
- Learned the main command terms used in your subjects
- Completed retrieval and question practice in every subject
- Started recording mistakes rather than merely checking scores
- Understood your school's immediate expectations for TOK, CAS, and the Extended Essay
- Identified a teacher, coordinator, or tutor you can approach
- Protected a realistic stopping time for sleep


The first month is about building control, not displaying endurance.


### The workload feels different before it becomes heavy


During the opening weeks, the challenge is often fragmentation. A reading task in English, a mathematics problem set, language vocabulary, a science write-up, and a TOK prompt may be manageable separately. Together, they create the sensation that something is always unfinished.


That feeling does not automatically mean you chose the wrong programme. It usually means your previous planning system was designed for fewer simultaneous responsibilities.


Use one master calendar rather than separate mental lists. Add tests, draft checkpoints, CAS commitments, school events, and rest. RevisionDojo's guide to[IB time management strategies](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/time-management-strategies-for-ib-students) offers a practical framework for making broad intentions visible.


Convert each entry into a clear next action. “Study chemistry” is vague. “Answer eight atomic structure questions and correct them” is easier to begin and finish.


Comic about organizing knowledge during DP1


### Your classes will teach assessment language


The IB Diploma includes six subjects alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subjects are graded from 1-7. TOK and the Extended Essay can contribute up to three additional points, while CAS must be completed successfully but does not receive points.


In your first month, the more useful question is how marks are earned in each classroom.


Teachers may introduce command terms such as *identify* , *explain* , *compare* , *discuss* , and *evaluate* . These are instructions, not decoration. An accurate explanation can remain incomplete if the question asks for evaluation. A long paragraph can waste time when the task requires only identification.


After marked work, record three things:


Question What to record


What did I misunderstand? The missing concept, method, fact, or instruction


Why did I lose marks? Knowledge, interpretation, structure, precision, or timing


What will I do next? One correction followed by a new attempt


This turns feedback into a reusable system. The[RevisionDojo IB resources hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) supports the process with subject-specific Study Notes, Flashcards, and Questionbank practice.


### The IB DP1 fall term may create subject doubts


It is normal for an HL subject to feel unexpectedly demanding. HL courses have greater scope than their SL counterparts, so the difference may appear through additional content, faster pacing, or more demanding assessments.


Do not judge a subject from one difficult lesson. Equally, do not ignore several weeks of evidence. Before requesting a change, ask whether you lack repairable prerequisite knowledge, whether the difficulty comes from content or assessment technique, and whether the subject supports your likely university plans.


Discuss concerns with the teacher and DP coordinator. Schools control timetables and deadlines for changing subjects, so another student's experience may not apply to you. Act early enough to preserve options, but gather evidence first. For broader context, consult the[IB subject revision guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/the-ultimate-ib-subject-guide-specific-revision-tips-for-every-course) .


### TOK, CAS, and the Extended Essay move at different speeds


The core can sound like three large projects arriving simultaneously. In practice, schools introduce these components on different schedules.


TOK may begin immediately. Expect questions about evidence, perspective, certainty, interpretation, and how knowledge is produced. You do not need to sound abstract. A strong early contribution can begin with a concrete example and examine what it does or does not justify.


CAS should become part of your routine rather than a future administrative rescue mission. Learn how your school records experiences, evidence, and reflections. Choose activities that suit your interests and timetable. Continuity and thoughtful reflection matter more than constructing an impressive-looking list.


Your school may introduce the Extended Essay during DP1, but you may not need a final research question in September. It is an independent research paper of up to 4,000 words, so a narrow, researchable question eventually matters more than a grand topic. For now, notice subjects that sustain your curiosity and follow your school's timeline.


### Your first assessments are diagnostic, not prophetic


A low first grade can feel like a verdict because the IB's 1-7 scale is unfamiliar. Treat it as information instead.


Ask where the marks disappeared. Did you misunderstand the content or command term? Did you run out of time? Was your evidence relevant but insufficiently explained? More rereading will not solve every problem.


Use a simple correction cycle:


1. Clarify one concept with concise Study Notes.
2. Retrieve the idea without looking.
3. Apply it through a short Questionbank set.
4. Classify each error.
5. Attempt a similar problem after a delay.


The guide to[starting strongly with RevisionDojo in DP1](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-for-ib-dp1-students) explains how to establish this loop without trying every resource at once.


### Build an intentionally modest study routine


Elaborate schedules can look reassuring, but they often collapse when a laboratory session runs late or a deadline moves. Begin with a flexible baseline:


Frequency Practical action


Most school days Complete 10-15 minutes of recall or Flashcards


Three times each week Pair focused review with Questionbank practice


Once each week Review errors and repeat selected questions


Once each week Complete one small TOK, CAS, EE, or coursework action


Every Sunday Check deadlines and choose three priorities


This is guidance, not an IB requirement. Adjust it around your health, commute, activities, and teachers' expectations. The[balanced IB study schedule](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-create-a-balanced-ib-study-schedule) provides a fuller weekly structure.


RevisionDojo is most valuable in DP1 when it reduces friction. Use **Study Notes** for unclear concepts, **Flashcards** for retrieval, and the **Questionbank** to expose weaknesses that reading can hide. Ask **AI Chat** focused questions, then reproduce the reasoning independently. As assessed work develops, use **Grading tools** , the **Coursework Library** , and **Tutors** for more targeted support. **Predicted Papers** and **Mock Exams** become more useful later for timed preparation.


The[RevisionDojo app workflow](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-app-ib-exam-prep) connects these tools into a repeatable learn, retrieve, apply, and correct cycle.


### What should feel different by November


By November, you should not expect to feel finished. You should expect to feel more oriented. You should know where deadlines live, how teachers communicate feedback, which subjects need attention, and what different command terms demand. CAS should have a workable rhythm, while TOK should feel less mysterious.


Most importantly, a disappointing mark should produce a next step rather than panic. The programme has not become easy. You have become less surprised by it. RevisionDojo can remain the central IB resource behind that transition, helping you start small, examine the evidence, and improve your routine before increasing your hours.
